thread:
jordan: Attempting the CLI quickstart inside a Docker container; first API call returns 502. The same token used in the dashboard succeeds.

jordan: docker command: `docker run --rm -e REDWOOD_API_KEY=$REDWOOD_API_KEY sample/quickstart`

jordan: Response:
```
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
content-type: text/html

<html>502 Bad Gateway</html>
```

sam: Is that a workspace token or a service key? 502 usually means routing/proxy.
jordan: Workspace token. Tried a service key and got 403; workspace token -> 502.
rachel: We've seen corp proxies strip `Authorization`. If header is removed the SDK retries and upstream routing can return 502 instead of 402/401.
onboard-bot: Your org (acme-sandbox) does not have an active billing method. First outbound requests may be gated. https://console.redwood.ai/orgs/acme-sandbox/billing
jordan: Weird — dashboard quickstart looked like it accepted the token.
sam: Try curl from your host: `curl -i https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" -d '{"input":"hi"}'`
jordan: From host I get 402 Payment Required `{\"error\":\"org_billing_required\"}`; in Docker it shows 502.
rachel: Confirmed header stripping + proxy rewrite. Workaround: mount token as a file and inject it inside the container or pass it with `-e REDWOOD_API_KEY=$(cat ~/.redwood/service_key)`.
sam: Action items: 1) eng/devex to add doc about proxies stripping Authorization, 2) CLI/SDK should detect this pattern (map 502->billing hint) and show actionable text, 3) improve dashboard UX to surface org billing state during quickstart.
jordan: Filing the ticket with minimal Dockerfile and steps, attaching curl outputs and headers. tagging @sam @rachel. thanks! :thumbsup:
